requirements.title: Control cannot transfer into a block from outside except for a return from an invoked procedure
requirements.source: 11.1.2.1 p1 first sentence; J3/24-007 PDF p203.
requirements.definition: Transfer of control from outside a block to a statement in the block is prohibited. The exception is the return from a procedure that was invoked within the block. Branching constructs, labels, and procedure return semantics are separate dependencies.

requirements.title: Transfers within a block and transfers from a block to outside are permitted forms
requirements.source: 11.1.2.1 p1 final sentence; J3/24-007 PDF p203.
requirements.definition: The language permits transfers within a block and transfers from the interior of a block to outside the block, subject to the branch, RETURN, EXIT, CYCLE, and construct-specific rules that own those transfers. review_rationale: batch111: independent fresh-context source review against pinned J3/24-007 (sha256 7371e889...). This batch opens Clause 11, so it establishes the shape later Clause 11 packets follow. The reviewer read all 44 base units of 11.1.1 Blocks, 11.1.2.1 Control flow in blocks, 11.1.2.2 Execution of a block, 11.1.3.1 through 11.1.3.4 the ASSOCIATE construct, and 11.1.4 the BLOCK construct in the original PDF rather than the author summary, verifying the titles from the source and confirming 44 base / 77 fine units, 42 requirements and 119 facets (all pending). The accounting claim was verified independently: the 20 numbered items R1101 in 11.1.1, R1102 through R1106 with C1101 through C1106 in 11.1.3.1, and R1107 through R1110 with C1107 through C1110 in 11.1.4 were already inventoried, so 24 non-numbered units are newly accounted, with no double count and no drop. Five permissions were adjudicated and accepted, including the 11.1.4 p3 explicit processor latitude for specification-expression evaluation order, which carries no plan asserting the processor took a particular order. Critically, the sentences of the form it is permissible to branch to an end statement only from within its construct do two things at once, permitting the inward branch and through the word only prohibiting the outward one, and the reviewer confirmed the packet captures both halves rather than losing a restriction or a permission. The attribution table was audited in full: all 30 negative rows were checked, including the R1109 row whose prohibiting words are a grammar production rather than a shall, the seven C1107 rows drawn from one prohibition list covering COMMON, EQUIVALENCE, INTENT, NAMELIST, OPTIONAL, statement functions and VALUE, the three C1101 rows and the four rows filed under 11.1.3.3 p5 that quote long compound sentences, confirming each negative isolates exactly one clause. The author's decision to treat C1104 as source-classification only was independently examined and accepted, because ordinary pointer assignment is conforming through the variable selector alternative, and 11.1.3.4's zero facets were accepted because its single note base unit and fine unit remain accounted. Decision: source-eligible, no blocking findings. This registers source accounting only: it is not fixture approval, it supplies no execution, and it approves no oracle.
